paragraphs: The honour box worked because taking more than one paper was pointless. It is one of the few retail mechanisms ever built that relied entirely on the product being worthless in quantity, and it disappeared the moment the news moved.
The model is light at 24,899 polygons and 25,516 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits urban and period visualisation, street furniture scenes, film and television backgrounds, game environments, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The domed lid is the detail that makes a chest read as treasure rather than as storage. Flat topped boxes stack, and a chest that cannot be stacked was never meant to be one of many, which is the whole implication.
The model is dense at 931,674 polygons and 911,116 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied open. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits game environments and props, film and television sets, fantasy and adventure illustration, museum material, advertising and editorial work. On sale since 2023.

Festoon lighting changed outdoor hospitality more than any piece of furniture. A line of warm bulbs overhead defines a space that has no walls, and every terrace, courtyard and pop up bar has been using that trick ever since.
The model holds 361,390 polygons and 183,290 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits exterior and hospitality visualisation, event and wedding scenes, architectural renders, advertising, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2026.

The cockerel on a church spire is older than most of the churches. It was mandated in parts of medieval Europe as a symbol, and it survived on farms and barns long after anybody remembered why the bird in particular.
The model is light at 19,162 polygons and 19,174 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 5 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits architectural and rural visualisation, heritage and period scenes, decor and product imagery, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The rotary shaver is a design that only one company ever committed to, and it exists because faces are curved. Three heads floating independently follow a jaw in a way a straight foil cannot, which is why the two systems never converged.

The model is very light at 10,152 polygons and 10,719 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 8 maps all at 2048x2048, with the trimmer attachment. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits product and grooming visualisation, e-commerce and packaging imagery, advertising, bathroom and interior scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

Wire ramps are the part of a pinball table that makes the noise everybody remembers. A ball running along two rails at speed is audible from across a room, and designers use that sound as deliberately as they use the lights.
The set holds 39,716 polygons and 40,178 vertices, built in quads only with mixed UV layout, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits arcade and leisure visualisation, game and machine component presentation, retro interiors, film props, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The squeezy lemon is a piece of packaging that became a permanent kitchen object. It looks like fruit, sits in the door of a fridge and has outlived several attempts to replace it with something more honest about what is inside.
The model is extremely light at 3,170 polygons and 1,593 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a green build is offered separately.
At $39 it suits food and packaging visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, kitchen and interior scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

A slot machine is an interface designed by people who understand attention better than most software companies. Everything on the cabinet, the height of the screen, the sound and the button placement, is arranged around keeping somebody seated.
The model is light at 26,785 polygons and 28,663 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits casino and leisure visualisation, gaming equipment marketing, interior scenes, film and television sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A pool hoist is the difference between a facility being accessible and merely claiming to be. It is required by law in many places, rarely photographed in brochures, and it is the single piece of equipment that decides whether some people can swim at all.

The model is light at 22,238 polygons and 22,129 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and rigged builds are offered separately, including native rigs for Maya and Cinema 4D.

At $39 it suits accessibility and facilities visualisation, pool and leisure centre scenes, equipment marketing, architectural renders, training material and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The portable extractor is the machine that turns a spill into a job that takes ten minutes rather than a professional visit. It sprays, agitates and sucks back in one pass, and everything about the design is about being carried up stairs.
The model is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits appliance and product visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, interior and cleaning scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A cool box works by having nothing to do. There is no mechanism, no power and no moving part: it is insulation around a mass of ice, and the entire performance figure is how slowly that ice is allowed to become water.
The model holds 106,862 polygons and 108,911 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, filled with ice. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits outdoor and lifestyle visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, picnic and event scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The parcel locker solved the last problem in delivery: somebody has to be at home. A wall of doors in a supermarket car park is a worse experience than a courier and a far better one than a missed delivery card, which is all it ever needed to be.

The model is extremely light at 5,166 polygons and 5,619 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps, 6 at 4096x4096 and one at 512x512. It carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits retail and logistics visualisation, urban and interior scenes, equipment marketing, interface mockups, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2020.

A workshop charger has to answer two questions: will this battery take a charge, and is it the battery at all. The tester half is the valuable part, because replacing a good battery is the most common wrong diagnosis in the trade.

The model is light at 36,146 polygons and 38,285 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and further builds of the unit are offered separately.
At $39 it suits garage and workshop visualisation, automotive equipment marketing, e-commerce imagery, training material, film props and game environments. On sale since 2021.

A converted container is a building with a delivery date rather than a construction schedule. The wide door is the modification that matters: a standard container opens at one end only, which is useless for anything a person walks in and out of.
The model holds 64,710 polygons and 70,365 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in red, and carries StemCell certification. A green build is offered separately.
At $39 it suits site and modular architecture visualisation, industrial and urban scenes, property presentation, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.
